# Reclassification of the imported cases

<!-- Generated by scripts/migrate/import-cases.mjs 2.0.0. Do not edit; run `npm run migrate:cases`. -->

Source: `redact-secret/redact-secret-benchmarks` at `1020d2b5905e8973098235e57c4cdca3359bba57` (read-only). This is stage B of issue #12 (part of #1). It says, for each of the 1,926 cases the first import (issue #4) wrote, whether it was a genuine Case, a reusable Scenario or a cell of a matrix projection, by which rule, and what the canonical tree looks like as a result. The criteria are ADR 0007 section 3; the decisions that stage B adds are in `docs/decisions/0008-semantic-tree-and-reclassification.md`.

The classification is a pure function of the legacy data and two authored tables (`scripts/migrate/lib/classify.mjs`: carrier groups; `scripts/migrate/authored/cases.mjs`: the groups each hand-written Case carries). There is no per-record decision: the rules below are the decision, and the run fails if a legacy group matches none.

## Result

|  | Before (first import) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cases (`records/cases/`) | 1,925 | 52 |
| Scenarios (`records/scenarios/`) | 0 | 29 |
| Fixture plans (`records/fixture-plans/`) | 0 | 5 |
| Fixture sets (`records/fixtures/`) | 67 (one per legacy suite) | 98 (one per provider, authored and generated apart) |
| Fixtures | 5,950 | 5,950 |
| Legacy-map entries (`migration/legacy-map/`) | 0 | 7,943 |
| Canonical ids or paths with a legacy coordinate | 1,992 | 0 |

The ADR 0007 target was: case count drops to genuine case studies, every fixture stays traceable. Both hold: 1,926 imported cases become 52 Cases (a 97.3% reduction), and 5,950 of 5,950 fixtures are mapped one to one to a fixture id in `migration/legacy-map/`.

## What each legacy case became

| Class | Legacy cases | Fixtures | Becomes | Canonical records |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| genuine Case | 61 | 327 | a Case, with hand-authored prose | 52 Cases (9 legacy groups folded into another Case of the same reasoning or tier) |
| reusable Scenario | 25 | 120 | a carrier Scenario; the fixtures are cells of it | 10 Scenarios |
| matrix projection | 1,840 | 5,503 | cells of a role Scenario; the per-cell prose is dropped | 17 Scenarios |
| total | 1,926 | 5,950 |  |  |

The 1,840 matrix projections (95.5% of the cases, 5,503 fixtures) are the template-worded cells the first import mistook for reasoning units: each was "Family name, role template" and differed from its neighbours only in the family's name, prefix or length.

## Rules

Rules are tried in this order; the first that applies decides. A legacy group that no rule covers stops the import.

| Rule | Class | Applies to | Legacy cases | Fixtures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `unsettled-evidence` | projection | Unresolved evidence (legacy tier T0) | 14 | 47 |
| `carrier-scenario` | scenario | Hand-written carrier narrative | 25 | 120 |
| `authored-case` | case | Hand-written narrative about a specific failure mode | 61 | 327 |
| `twin-projection` | projection | One-property twin of a positive | 532 | 1,372 |
| `control-projection` | projection | Benign control of a family | 760 | 1,323 |
| `positive-projection` | projection | Documented-format positive of a family | 316 | 2,186 |
| `lookalike-projection` | projection | Benign lookalike of a family | 218 | 575 |

### `unsettled-evidence`

The legacy benchmark left these fixtures unscored. A case asserts an expectation, and there is none to assert: the inputs become cells of the scenario `unsettled-evidence-input`, which exists to keep the open question visible. Applied first, to every role.

### `carrier-scenario`

The suite's own prose is about a carrier or an input edge (quoting, line endings, multibyte text), states one sentence of reasoning that holds for every format, and differs between families only by the family's name. ADR 0007 criterion 3 fails (a scenario plus a family list reproduces it), so it is a Scenario; its fixtures are cells of a family x scenario plan.

### `authored-case`

The suite's prose names a failure mode that is specific to it (a documented example value one character off, a placeholder vocabulary boundary, a key at the end of a line, a mask ending in a real character, a format with trailing punctuation) and cannot be produced by substituting a family name into a template. It has its own expectation and a stated reason for it. Groups that state the same reasoning, or that differ only in evidence tier, fold into one Case.

### `twin-projection`

A twin's only content is which single property of a positive was changed (length, prefix, alphabet, boundary, carrier marker, checksum, public prefix) for which family. That sentence is the same for every family, so it is a cell of the matching twin scenario. The fixture keeps its `twin-of` lineage to the exact positive fixture. Applies to twins in hand-written suites too: their narrative adds nothing beyond the property.

### `control-projection`

A control (public identifier, placeholder, reference, near miss, encoded value, prose mention) is worded from a per-type template plus the family name. The type is the scenario; the family is the cell. A control type whose outcome is must-flag (a provider-format near miss that the project still reports because it sits under a credential-named assignment) is the scenario `credential-named-literal-near-miss`.

### `positive-projection`

A positive base group of a generated suite states only that a value built to the family's documented format, in some carriers, must be flagged. That is the scenario `documented-format-literal` for one family; the carriers are the fixtures' `context`.

### `lookalike-projection`

A benign base group of a generated suite (bare prefix, mask, short body, label prose, embedding) is worded from a template plus the family name. It is the scenario `benign-lookalike` for one family.

## Evidence tier is not identity

The first import keyed a case on suite, shape, role, outcome **and legacy tier**. 121 of the 1,799 keys that differ only in tier were split across two or three cases (248 cases); those merge: a tier never creates a Case, a Scenario or a plan cell. The tier, re-expressed as an evidence basis, is carried per fixture in the set's `evidence` map (with the reason and sources the legacy assessment cited), and a Case or Scenario states only the weakest basis its fixtures share.

| Fixtures by evidence basis | Count |
| --- | --- |
| `provider-documented` | 1,308 |
| `tool-corroborated` | 2,277 |
| `project-policy` | 2,318 |
| `unresolved` | 47 |

| Cases by expectation basis (weakest of their fixtures) | Count |
| --- | --- |

| `project-policy` | 46 |
| `unresolved` | 0 |

1 Case carries fixtures of more than one basis (`sendgrid-near-miss-values`); its fixtures keep their own evidence entries.

Criteria applied (ADR 0007 section 3): a failure mode specific to the Case, prose no template could produce, an expectation that no Scenario plus a family list reproduces, its own evidence or an explicit project-policy decision, and a name without a coordinate. Borderline decisions, stated so they can be disputed:

- The nine carrier groups of the context-edges suite and the four carrier groups of token-contexts are **Scenarios**, not Cases: their narrative is about the carrier, and the same sentence holds for every format. Criterion 3 fails for them.

- Twins (one-property mutations) are **matrix projections** even in hand-written suites (SendGrid, policy-qualified credentials, context-edges, token-contexts): the twin's content is the changed property and the family. The fixture keeps its `twin-of` lineage to the exact positive.

- Milestone regressions, reference-syntax groups and their overlaps fold together: a reasoning unit stated in two suites (code expressions, secret-manager pointers, template expressions, interpolation, literals under generic names) is one Case.

- A positive group and its benign counterpart stay two Cases: a Case has one outcome, and the pairing is the reasoning (the exemption and its boundary).

## Every fixture is traceable

`migration/legacy-map/<suite>.json` has one shard per legacy suite (67 shards, 7,943 entries): the suite, each imported case and each fixture, with the canonical record that carries it. No entry is `dropped`: nothing was removed. The map is what lets the compatibility exporter regenerate legacy names (stage C) and lets a consumer trace any of the 5,950 legacy fixtures. The legacy fixture id of a fixture appears only there.

Fixture ids are `<provider>--<name>`: the provider set plus the legacy fixture name with any migration coordinate removed (92 names were scrubbed) and a deterministic suffix when two legacy suites used one name (28 collisions).

## Incidents and lineage

The 63 known-gap issues of the legacy repository attach to 7 Cases and, for fixtures that are now matrix cells, to 138 fixtures directly (`incidents` on the set item; a cell has no record of its own to hold them). Twin lineage is fixture level: 1,391 twin fixtures keep `lineage.of` to the exact positive fixture; case-level `twin-of` relations were a property of the legacy groups and are not recreated (the twin groups are scenario cells now).

## Determinism

`npm run migrate:cases` reads only the pinned legacy revision (through `git archive`, running the legacy generators over that extraction and checking each corpus against the legacy hash manifest) and the committed taxonomy records. `npm run migrate:cases -- --check` regenerates everything in memory and fails on any difference in the owned directories or in this report.
